\smallskip Drafts are in \textcolor{draft}{blue}; black is the designer's glyph. Each letter is drafted from the style's own letters where the regular glyph shows how the designer built it:
\begin{description}\setlength\itemsep{0pt}\small
\item[Method (rebuilt 2026-11-13)] Every draft is built from components, as a font source builds a glyph: the base letter's own contours, plus a part that is a glyph of the font or one simple contour, or a splice of two contours. No boolean operations: the drafts keep the components' own points and \emph{overlap} where the components overlap (FontForge shows them unmerged; font generation merges them). In regular the designer built most of these letters the same way: Ɇ\,=\,E\,+\,U+0338 (0.2\,\% mismatch), Ɍ\,=\,R\,+\,U+0335, ẝ\,=\,ſ\,+\,U+0335, Ɉ\,=\,J\,+\,U+0336, …
\item[overlay] Ɍ Ɏ ɏ ẝ ꞓ ỻ: the base and the style's own stroke overlay mark (U+0335 or U+0336), scaled to the bar's length and the style's bar thickness (own Đ, Ƚ or đ), placed as the mark fits in the designer's glyph: its height, and its offset from the stem (or the de-slanted centre).
\item[reference] Ɇ: E and the long solidus U+0338 (redrawn in semibold and semibold italic, where it was the short one), crossing half E's height 23 left of E's de-slanted centre. Ⅎ Ɐ Ʌ: turned references.
\item[part] ẜ ꝥ: the base and the stroke of regular's glyph as one contour (ẜ's a rectangle, ꝥ's with its swelling ends), slanted and thickened to the style.
\item[splice] Ɱ (M and J's hook), ꭒ (u and ɿ's fishhook), ỿ (y and regular's ỿ loop), ɋ (q's own descender and ʈ's hook, regular ɽ's, at the descender), Ɉ (italic J, its own crossbar spliced out, + U+0336), Ỻ (I and L cut where their serifs overlap and joined, as regular's: one outline and the counter between the stems), Ɋ (regular's Ɋ, its bowl spliced from the style's O, its tail lengthened by splicing it with itself moved down): the outlines are cut where they cross a line and joined there; points left on a straight edge are dropped.
\item[reduced] ᵝ ᵞ ᵟ: the style's own β γ δ, de-slanted, scaled to the box of regular's modifier at its height and side bearings, and pushed outward or inward to the weight of regular's modifier times the style's ᵛ over regular's ᵛ (the designer's own superscript weights: italic 0.89, semibold 1.13, semibold italic 1.12). Regular's are drawn apart from β γ δ, not reduced (the recipe check below). Second row: regular's modifier, slanted (as the designer's italic ᵛ is regular's) and in the semibold styles pushed outward by stage 3's rule.
\item[copy] ᵜ (a superscript U+1D25 ain, which no style has): regular's, as the second row of ᵝ ᵞ ᵟ; the spacing modifiers ˪ ˫ ˯--˿: the lighter style's, pushed outward.
\end{description}
Each cell shows the base letter, the letter, and a letter of the same style with the analogous part. \section*{Control points of the drafts}
Every draft as compiled into \verb|fonts/*-draft.otf| (what FontForge shows on opening them), beside the designer's regular glyph: on-curve points black, off-curve points as open circles on their handles. The components overlap, unmerged, as in a font source. The dashed line is a splice's joining height (on the designer's regular glyph, where the recipe joins when it is run in regular); at a splice, points left on a straight edge are dropped.\par\medskip

\section*{Recipe checks in regular}
The recipes that take a part from another letter, run in regular and compared with the designer's glyph (in the regular draft font at U+F600 and up). Mismatch: the ink of designer XOR recipe, at the same origin, over the designer's ink; a shift of the whole letter counts double on a thin letter (once where ink is missing, once where it is extra), so the mismatch after the best horizontal shift is given too.\par
